welcome.title: Welcome to Satohash
welcome.subtitle: Turn your important agreements into cryptographic proof that they existed at a specific time—anchored to Bitcoin and easy to verify.
welcome.pricingNote: Satohash is currently free while we're in early access. You only pay the Bitcoin network fee when you timestamp a document.

features.cryptoProofDesc: Create an unforgeable fingerprint of your document using SHA-256 cryptography.
features.cryptoProofDetail: Hashing converts any file into a unique 64-character string. Even a single changed comma results in a completely different hash. Satohash handles this locally on your device.
features.timestampDesc: Anchor your proof to the Bitcoin blockchain using the OpenTimestamps protocol.
features.timestampDetail: Your document's hash is bundled with thousands of others into a Merkle tree. A single 'root' hash is then committed to the Bitcoin network, providing permanent, immutable proof of existence.
features.verifyDesc: Anyone can verify your proof independently using open-source tools.
features.verifyDetail: A .ots file contains the 'path' from your document to the Bitcoin block. You don't need Satohash to prove it; you can use the official OpenTimestamps client or third-party block explorers.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.subtitle: Three simple steps to protect your documents

card1.title: Lock in the date
card1.description: Satohash gives your document a unique fingerprint and locks its date into the Bitcoin network. Later, anyone can check that this exact document existed at that time.

card2.title: Your content stays private
card2.description: We don't need to see your full document. We only use a cryptographic fingerprint, not the text itself.

card3.title: Easy to prove later
card3.description: You get a PDF and a small proof file. Even without Satohash, you or your lawyer can verify it using open tools.

chooseTemplate.title: What do you want to protect today?
chooseTemplate.disclaimer: You can edit every template. Satohash does not give legal advice; we help you lock in the evidence.

explain.title: What does timestamping do?
explain.description: Satohash will create a cryptographic fingerprint of this document and send it to the Bitcoin network using an open standard called OpenTimestamps. This proves that this exact document existed before a certain time, without revealing its contents.
explain.point1: We do not upload your document to the blockchain, only the fingerprint.
explain.point2: Later, anyone can verify the proof using open tools, not just Satohash.
explain.point3: If the document changes, the fingerprint and proof no longer match.
explain.feeDescription: This fee goes to Bitcoin miners, not Satohash. It changes with network activity.

progress.title: Creating your timestamp…
progress.info: This usually takes a few seconds to submit, and up to a few hours to be fully confirmed by the Bitcoin network. You can already download a receipt, and Satohash will upgrade it to a full proof once the network confirms.

result.title: Your timestamp is created
result.statusPending: Proof status: Pending blockchain confirmation (early receipt)
result.statusComplete: Proof status: Confirmed on Bitcoin blockchain
result.keepSafe: Keep this proof package somewhere safe. Even if Satohash disappeared, you could still verify that this exact document existed before this time using open-source tools.

verificationHelp.title: How to verify this later
verificationHelp.withSatohashDesc: Upload your PDF and proof file here. We'll check it against the Bitcoin network and tell you if everything matches.
verificationHelp.withoutSatohashDesc: You can use any OpenTimestamps-compatible tool to verify your proof. Upload your original document and the .ots proof file. The tool will tell you whether the fingerprint matches and when it was anchored into Bitcoin.
verificationHelp.noMatchDesc: If the proof doesn't verify, it usually means the document was changed or the wrong file was used.

trust.title: Trust Center
trust.howItWorksDetail: Satohash uses the SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit) to create a unique digital fingerprint of your document. This happens locally in your browser; your document's text never needs to leave your device. This hash is then bundled with thousands of others into a Merkle Tree and its root is anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain using the OpenTimestamps protocol. This creates a permanent, immutable record of existence.
trust.whatBlockchainDetail: Blockchain timestamping provides mathematical proof that a specific dataset existed at a specific time and has not been altered. It does NOT prove the identity of the signer by itself (requires additional verification), it does NOT guarantee the legal correctness of the contract contents, and it CANNOT be modified or deleted once anchored. It is a 'proof of existence' tool, not a substitute for legal review.
trust.zkPrivacyDetail: Our 'Privacy Shield' technology is inspired by Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs. Because we only store the cryptographic hash of your document, we have zero knowledge of its contents. Using Merkle inclusion proofs, we can even allow you to selectively redact sensitive parts of a document while still proving the remaining parts match the original anchored version—providing both absolute privacy and absolute verifiability.
trust.legallyBindingDetail: In many jurisdictions, cryptographic evidence is recognized under laws like the ESIGN Act (US), UETA (US), and eIDAS (EU). These frameworks generally state that an electronic record should not be denied legal effect solely because it is in electronic form. Blockchain timestamps provide an extremely high tier of 'Electronic Time-Stamps' and 'Electronic Evidence' that can be used in court to rebut claims of document forgery or backdating.
trust.legalDisclaimer: Satohash provides evidence and tooling, not legal advice. Users must consult local law and counsel.
